nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty standard Borel space, $\mu$ a finite measure on $\alpha$, and $X : \alpha \to \beta$, $Y : \alpha \to \Omega$ measurable maps. Then the conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$ under $\mu$, the kernel from $\beta$ to $\Omega$ obtained by disintegrating the joint law of $(X, Y)$ under $\mu$, is a regular conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$ under $\mu$.
nodes.title: The conditional distribution kernel is a regular conditional distribution

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty standard Borel space, $\mu$ a finite measure on a measurable space $(\alpha, \mathcal{F})$, $\mathcal{G} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$ a sub-σ-algebra, and $Y : \alpha \to \Omega$ an $\mathcal{F}$-measurable map. Then some family of measures on $\Omega$ indexed by $\alpha$ is a measure-valued regular conditional distribution of $Y$ given $\mathcal{G}$ under $\mu$.
nodes.title: Existence of measure-valued regular conditional distributions given a sub-σ-algebra

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty standard Borel space, $\mu$ a finite measure on $\alpha$, and $X : \alpha \to \beta$, $Y : \alpha \to \Omega$ measurable maps. Then some family of measures on $\Omega$ indexed by $\alpha$ is a measure-valued regular conditional distribution of $Y$ given the σ-algebra $\sigma(X)$ on $\alpha$ generated by $X$, under $\mu$.
nodes.title: Existence of measure-valued regular conditional distributions given a random variable

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty standard Borel space, $\mu$ a finite measure on $\alpha$, and $X : \alpha \to \beta$, $Y : \alpha \to \Omega$ measurable maps. Then there exists a kernel $\kappa$ from $\beta$ to $\Omega$ that is a regular conditional distribution of $Y$ given $X$ under $\mu$; in particular $\kappa$ is a Markov kernel.
nodes.title: Existence of regular conditional distributions (kernel form)

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\alpha$ and let $X : \alpha \to \beta$ and $Y : \alpha \to \Omega$ be maps. nodes.title: Regular conditional distribution (kernel form)

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
